candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: use infection-control and microbiologic information to support safe, evidence-based care and antimicrobial stewardship.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — interpreting facility antibiograms
candidate.educational_objective: Use the hospital antibiogram as an aggregate summary of local organism-antibiotic susceptibility patterns to inform empiric therapy while still incorporating infection site, patient factors, and patient-specific culture/susceptibility results when available.

options.A: Aggregate local susceptibility percentages for organism-antimicrobial combinations that can help guide empiric antibiotic selection.
options.B: The current patient's individual allergy history and prior adverse drug reactions.
options.C: A definitive susceptibility result for the current patient's infecting organism before that organism has been cultured.
options.D: Hospital medication acquisition costs without microbiologic susceptibility information.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. CDC's NHSN Antimicrobial Resistance guidance describes a facility-wide antibiogram as a table of calculated percent susceptible values for organism-antimicrobial combinations and states that antibiogram data can be used to guide empirical antimicrobial therapy. B is patient-specific history, not antibiogram data. C overstates what aggregate surveillance can provide; the antibiogram does not replace patient-specific culture and susceptibility testing. D describes financial information rather than a microbiology susceptibility summary.
candidate.source_claim_supported: A hospital antibiogram summarizes aggregate local antimicrobial susceptibility percentages and can inform empiric antimicrobial selection, but it is not an individual patient's susceptibility test.
candidate.source_document_title: FAQs: Antimicrobial Resistance (AR) Option; MDRO Management — Summary of Recommendations
candidate.source_locator: NHSN AR Option FAQ Q9: facility-wide antibiogram displays calculated percent susceptible (%S) for each organism-antimicrobial combination; NHSN/CLSI antibiograms can be used to guide selection of empirical antimicrobial therapy. MDRO Management V.A.3.a: hospitals and LTCFs should review local susceptibility patterns (antibiograms) to foster appropriate antimicrobial use.
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), National Healthcare Safety Network
